title: loadWorld is the cheap path for a new client witness (markup option, one common.js route, one click helper, derived consumer list)
description:
## Goal

Writing a new client-test witness on the shared world (`loadWorld`, `createFakeDom`) is cheaper than writing a local stub. Then the census ratchet treats the cause, not only the symptom.

## Context

LIN-4255's close-out (LIN-4272) found the cause: a new witness still reaches for a local stub because `loadWorld` costs more to write than one. Four blind, code-only reads of the fake-DOM move, at `591bb9596`, and two Surveys of LIN-4292, at `af55cb737`, named the same friction. These are claims to check at this ticket's base:

* **No markup before scripts.** `loadWorld` runs its scripts before a caller can set the page markup (LIN-4289), so suites hand-run their loaders.
* **Three recipes for one setup.** There are three ways to load `common.js`'s harness models: `disclosureWindowStubs`; an inline `__HARNESS_MODELS__`; and `withHarnessModels` run by hand after `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })`. `loadWorld`'s JSDoc describes the choice rather than making it. The eight observation suites repeat one stub set.
* **The click helper is bypassed.** `clickOn` exists, but about six suites loop over `listenersOf('click')` themselves.
* **A hand-kept registry.** The `fake-dom.js` header keeps a list of about 35 consumers, tagged by ticket, and every move edits it. The census already knows who the consumers are. The `<select>` stop is written there as well as in the census comments.
* **A dead workaround.** `real-dispatch-disclosure.js`'s `browserMarkup` decodes `—`/`…`, which the fake already decodes.
* **Stop reasons are comments.** They sit on the census entries, which nothing asserts (LIN-4272's builder).

## This step

1. LIN-4289's `markup` option on `loadWorld`. Its hand-run call sites use it.
2. One named switch for the `common.js` harness-models route, in place of the three recipes.
3. Move the hand-written click loops onto `clickOn`.
4. Derive the fake's consumer list from the census, and delete the hand-kept copy and the dead decode.
5. Stop reasons become data the census asserts.
6. **Only then,** if it can be done without a new hand-kept list, a census signal that fails a new client-test file that vm-runs a `public/` script on a local stub.
   * Run the matcher over the tree first, and record what it catches.
   * Scope it to files that vm-run a `public/` script, not to `lin-` names.
   * Pin it with fixtures, and keep the existing NEGATIVE fixtures true.

## Done when

* A new witness copied from the nearest existing one would use `loadWorld`.
* There is one `common.js` route and one click helper.
* No hand-kept consumer list remains.
* Stop reasons are asserted.
* Every touched suite keeps its names and counts.
* `CLAUDE.md` stays within budget.

*Note (19:25): the dead* `browserMarkup` *decode and the stale line references go in LIN-4296.*

## From Drift & Coherence run 4 (`6c6bada5`, row 133, at `af55cb73`): the census can't see most of this

Of the 68 vm-over-`public/` suites, **64 don't use** `loadWorld`: 25 are census-listed hand-written fakes, 1 imports `fake-dom.js`, and **38 build their own non-tree** `document` **stub that the census excludes by design** (it matches a tree shape). So the witness-default problem is larger than the census shows, and step 6's check must decide what to do with those 38: grandfather them, or bring them under one rule. Either way, run the matcher over the tree first (Drift's figures are a claim to re-measure at this ticket's base).

*Notes (21:10):*

* **Item 4's consumer-list derivation moved to LIN-4254's first piece,** so its 16 moves don't hand-edit the list. The dead decode went in LIN-4296.
* **From LIN-4296's blind reads, for item 3 (one click helper):** the off-tree synthetic press (`contains = () => true` plus a fake button) is now written separately in `lin-3833-run-control` and `prompt-section-task-mode`, while `client-world.js` says `click`/`key` are its only shims. It wants a `pressOffTree` there.
* The `PROXY_PROMPT_BOX` regex cut of `renderProxyPage` is copied into `lin-3136` and `lin-4296-scope-pick`, which wants one shared fixture.
* Two stale comments: task-mode's "census stop for this suite", and the header's "listed in `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES`" for the former select stops.

*Note (21:20, from LIN-4304's blind reads):* step 6's census signal will be the sixth hand-rolled acorn walker in the source-shape tests. `fake-dom-census`, `llm-jobs-census`, `free-tier-model-clamp-wiring`, `lin-4080-*` and now `public-element-method-guards` each bring their own `parse`-with-fallback and child walker, though `acorn-walk` is already a dependency. If step 6 runs, **extract one shared walker into** `tests/unit/helpers/` **first**, and move the existing five onto it (for the census, keep its note about not importing another test file). Don't add a sixth copy.

comments.body: From the LIN-4296 close-out (ledger item 4): `browserMarkup` in `tests/unit/helpers/real-dispatch-disclosure.js` was deleted by PR #2317 (merged `b581ac92`), so drop the "dead workaround" bullet (line 14) from this ticket's list; the "note (19:25)" line already says it went to LIN-4296.

**Derived consumer list moved to LIN-4306 (LIN-4254 piece 0), PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2321.** Item 4 here (derived consumer list: the census computes the fake's importers instead of the header hand-keeping them) is built there: an AST `ImportDeclaration` scan finds the importers, and the header no longer lists them. The Done-when "No hand-kept consumer list remains" is met by that PR, once it merges. This ticket should not delete or re-add the computed list, and should not reassign the piece to itself.
